solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I attempt to catch a Shakespearean villain

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a go is an attempt, as in 'have a go'

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to capture the villain of a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: I and GO make the outer word, and A sits inside it, giving IAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming ensign who destroys Othello, the best-known villain in Shakespeare's tragedies.

clue.text: Scene with din could make one very angry

indicators.note: the words could be made into a single new word, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A noisy row could make a person furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Incensed means enraged, a stronger synonym of angry.

clue.text: Snide comment of American soldier beginning to blame English

parts.note: GI is the familiar term for a US soldier

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A US soldier makes a sneering remark that starts to blame the English.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibe is a taunting or insulting remark, a synonym for a snide comment.

clue.text: Artist is beginning to smile when hugged by chum

indicators.note: something hugged is wrapped in arms, so these letters sit inside another word

parts.note: a mate is a friend or chum

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

explanation.surface: A painter grins as a friend embraces him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist' tempts as the RA of crosswords, but here it is the definition, a painter named outright.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French painter famous for bold colour and paper cut-outs, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Mother isn't fussed about church service

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: fussing about means bustling around in agitation, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mum is unbothered about going to church.
explanation.definitionFit: Matins is the morning prayer service of the Anglican church, an example of a church service.

clue.text: Nasty prancer resolved to slide maybe

indicators.note: something resolved has been broken down and worked out afresh, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A spiteful horse decided to slip and skid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slide' looks like a verb; 'maybe' marks it as a noun example, a photographic slide.
explanation.definitionFit: A transparency is a positive image on film viewed by projection, and a photographic slide is one example.

clue.text: One protecting those that may get fleeced?

definitions.text: One protecting those that may get fleeced?

parts.words: One protecting those that may get fleeced
parts.note: surface reading: someone guarding likely victims of swindlers
setter's reading: sheared of wool, so the protected creatures are sheep and their guardian tends a flock

explanation.walkthrough: Fleeced sounds like cheated, but the question mark points to its literal sense of having the wool sheared off.
explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd guards and tends a flock, and sheep are the animals that get shorn of their fleece.

clue.text: Headless brute from the Orient

indicators.note: without a head means the first letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A decapitated monster arrives from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is an old name for the countries of Asia, which lie to the east of Europe.

clue.text: Awfully inhumane pop's gaining advantage unfairly?

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly and in a mess, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken with the S that follows it

explanation.surface: A cruel father is cheating to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'pop's' belongs to the fodder rather than standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: One-upmanship is the art of staying a step ahead of a rival, often by sly means; the question mark admits it is not always cheating.

clue.text: Prime ministers as skilled craftspeople?

parts.note: surface reading: heads of government, who appoint their senior ministers
setter's reading: joiners who build fine wooden furniture, whose trade name matches what a prime minister does when choosing ministers

explanation.walkthrough: A prime minister forms a cabinet of senior ministers; the trade name for furniture joiners describes exactly that, read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabinetmakers are craftsmen who build fine furniture, and a prime minister literally makes a government cabinet.

clue.text: Superior Navy vessel

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class or superior usage

explanation.surface: A top-class warship, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Navy vessel' reads as a ship, but vessel is the definition alone: a container.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase-like container, and any container may be called a vessel.

clue.text: Fasten components the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running backwards, so the word is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Instructions warning that the pieces have been fitted together incorrectly.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap something is to secure it with a band, a verb sense of fasten.

clue.text: Teacher (100!) to talk incessantly

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: A teacher shouting a hundred times seems to go on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit on is British slang for chattering endlessly; a ton is a hundred, as in a hundred runs or miles per hour.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is a British idiom for chattering at length about trivia.

clue.text: Fool that is not heartless may be seen as wise

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'
taken as written before losing its middle

explanation.surface: A fool who still has some feeling may be thought wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a literary adjective for having great wisdom, a synonym of wise.

clue.text: Len set us up? That's unpleasant to hear!

indicators.note: here only 'up' signals the change: things that are up are disturbed, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A man called Len has played a trick on us, and it grates.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuneless singing lacks melody, so it is grating on the ear.

clue.text: Band had sacked skilful worker

indicators.note: something sacked is ransacked and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A group of musicians fired their most talented member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' reads as dismissed from a job, but it signals a rearrangement. Dab hand is a British idiom for an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is someone very skilled at a task, an idiom for an expert worker.

clue.text: Head of sales in store is horribly powerful type

indicators.note: placed in means set inside, so this letter sits within the other word
the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

explanation.surface: The sales boss in a shop wields power horribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horribly' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a tyrant who holds absolute power and uses it cruelly.

clue.text: Artist and academic gas

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A painter and a scholar chat idly together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' looks like a verb for chatter; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, one example of a chemical element in gaseous form.

clue.text: You heard sheep

indicators.note: something heard is taken by ear, so the word's sound counts rather than its spelling

explanation.surface: Someone tells you that you heard the sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, a specific kind of the animal.

clue.text: Times thunders, putting out leader

indicators.note: putting out the leader means dropping the first letter

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper, nicknamed the Thunderer, writes a fiery leader column.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is called the Thunderer, and a leader is a newspaper editorial, so the surface is about journalism; here leader means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages are eras or periods, so the word is a synonym for times in the historical sense.

clue.text: Quiet river free from pollution

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A calm, clean river with no contamination.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure water or air is unadulterated, containing nothing that contaminates it.

clue.text: Understand instruction from editor to photographer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for grasping the situation
second meaning: read literally, an order to go out and obtain an image

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is the phrase taken literally, as a newspaper editor's order.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the picture is an idiom meaning to grasp what is going on, and literally it tells a photographer to fetch an image.

clue.text: Blemish on paper — it is dark against bright background

definitions.text: it is dark against bright background

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A mark on a newspaper page, dark against the bright white sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the first piece after the second, so the blemish follows the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunspot is a cooler region of the solar surface that appears dark against the brilliant photosphere around it.

clue.text: Insects — hear them in B&B

indicators.note: hearing something means taking its sound, so the letter names are said out loud

parts.note: the two letter Bs in the abbreviation, said out loud as letter names

explanation.surface: Guests at a bed and breakfast hear insects buzzing about.
explanation.walkthrough: B&B is short for bed and breakfast, a small guest house; the two Bs in it, read as letter names, make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees are flying insects that make honey, so they are examples of insects.
